notes: §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR11 holds the CLASS clause's literals to two rules: "If numeric, must be unsigned integers and must have a value within the range of one through the maximum number of characters in the native character set" and "If nonnumeric and associated with a THROUGH phrase, must each be one character in length". SwitchBindClass decodes every literal-4 and literal-5 through LiteralPhraseOperand at every edition (no edition arm; the rule's 2023 successor adds only the count cap, which SwitchBindClass asks under the IN phrase alone): an integer literal (IntegerLiteralDigits) is refused when signed and when its value is outside 1 through 65,536, the native character set docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-188 documents; a noninteger numeric literal is refused by the class rule; and under THROUGH OneCharacterOperands refuses each nonnumeric operand that is not one character, all with COBOL1671. Probed at 85: +66, -5 THRU 9, 0, 65537, a 20-digit integer, 1.5, 66 THRU 67.5 and "A" THRU "YZ" are refused; 65536, 66 THRU 67, 67 THROUGH "7", "Z" THRU "A" and the multi-character "B7" without THROUGH compile and the class test answers correctly. The witness is "AB" THROUGH "Z", refused with COBOL1671.

next.reason: 1985: "If numeric, must be unsigned integers and must have a value within the range of one through the maximum number of characters"; 2023: "The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native alphanumeric character set or". 2023 keeps the CLASS literal rules (unsigned integer in range, one-character THROUGH literals) but adds a cap on total characters specified, refusing programs 1985 accepted.
